notes:
Account background: mid-stage fintech (payments + risk), migrating several microservices to vector search + LLM scoring. Interested in Reserved (Dedicated) for predictable latency and cost. Security team insists on VPC private control plane and KMS-integration. Short timeline: POC in Mar, procurement in Apr if sizing matches TCO.

Sales thread summary (shorthand):
- 2026-02-01: Intro call (Maya) — interested in replacing legacy heuristics with LLM-based fraud scoring. Wants p95 < 200ms for scoring path.
- 2026-02-14: Technical deep-dive (Ethan) — shared sample QPS logs, token distribution, current avg payload ~120 tokens.
- 2026-02-21: Security kickoff (Renee) — sent SOC2 and IAM questionnaire; security asked for network flow diagrams.
- 2026-03-02: Pre-POC sync — agreed to run a dedicated sizing workshop; Infra to provide historical 30-day QPS heatmap.
- 2026-03-09: Workshop prep call — they requested cost/latency trade-off scenarios and fallback routing (hosted -> dedicated -> private).

POC / Workshop goals (from customer):
- Validate steady-state and burst capacity numbers for fraud scoring pipeline.
- Confirm p95 latency SLOs at target QPS and token distributions.
- Determine reserved GPU footprint for monthly commit vs autoscale burst capacity.
- Identify SLA language they'd require for enterprise contract.

Customer constraints & preferences (notes):
- Must keep raw transaction data in-region (US-East).
- Cannot send PHI to hosted endpoints; prefer private control plane and VPC peering.
- High cost sensitivity on per-token spend for embeddings and scoring.
- Prefer Redwood routing to fallback to a cheaper quantized variant during extended peaks.

Stated latency/throughput targets and sample numbers (customer-provided):
- Baseline steady QPS (business hours): 40 requests/sec (avg).
- Average tokens per scoring request: 120 tokens (inference only, no heavy context).
- Steady-state token/sec estimate: ~4,800 tokens/sec.
- Peak bursts observed (fraud spikes, ~15-40s): up to 380 requests/sec sustained for short windows.
- Peak token/sec estimate during burst: up to ~76,000 tokens/sec (avg burst tokens ~200).

Preliminary sizing notes (Redwood SE & Infra thinking):
- Target p95 <200ms for short-context scoring (<=256 tokens) requires dedicated low-latency configuration and conservative batching.
- Suggest reserved footprint for steady-state: 6x H100-equivalent GPUs to meet sustained 40 QPS with headroom for typical growth (includes KV cache priming and batching).
- Autoscale/burst plan: allow burst capacity to scale to 12-14 GPUs for short bursts (minutes) with automatic fallback to quantized model variant if queueing grows >100ms beyond SLO.
- Expected warm/KV cache behavior: initial priming may add latency for first 10-20 requests per model version; plan cache warm-up during deployment window.
- Cost tradeoffs: 6 reserved GPUs with burst pool reduces per-token cost vs fully autoscaled hosted but requires commit; we will run cost model in workshop.

Procurement & legal asks observed so far:
- Wants SLA that includes p95 latency targets for scoring endpoint, uptime 99.9% for dedicated pool, and credits for missed targets.
- Requires standard security addendum, KMS proof-of-concept, and audit logging retention to 1 year.

Open questions for workshop (to collect):
- Provide 30-day QPS heatmap sliced by hour and day-of-week. -> action: Orch infra to deliver by 2026-03-18.
- Provide representative traces for 95th percentile scoring requests (include tokens per request).
- Clarify acceptable RTO/RPO for failover to hosted model.

Quick next steps (AE/SE/CSM playbook):
- Send prework worksheet (QPS matrix + sample log template) — action Maya, due 2026-03-12.
- Run 2-hour sizing workshop with Redwood SEs (Ethan) + Infra + Security (Renee) during week of 2026-03-22.
- Produce 2 sizing scenarios (conservative vs cost-optimized) and a draft SLA term sheet for procurement review by 2026-03-29.
sizing_workshop_notes:
Workshop focus: translate QPS -> tokens/sec -> GPU equivalents; plan reserved vs burst pools; model variant routing for graceful degradation.

Workshop preliminary calc examples (for discussion):
- Steady: 40 QPS * 120 tokens = 4,800 tokens/sec -> target reserve: 6x H100-equivalent for p95<200ms with batching tuned.
- Peak burst: 380 QPS * 200 tokens = 76,000 tokens/sec -> autoscale to 12-14 GPUs, enable quantized fallback to reduce latency and queueing.
- Warm-up: KV priming window estimate 10-15k tokens with slightly higher latency; include cache pre-population step in deploy runbook.
- Throughput guarantees: propose committed throughput floor (tokens/sec) mapped to reserved GPUs in contract; define burst credits for occasional overage.

Negotiation points to prepare: SLA credit formulas, allowed maintenance windows, escalation path, data residency clause, minimum commit term, and options for quarterly re-sizing.
